body_json.answer:
**Assessment:** rejected.

The new post's broad skepticism toward "official accounts and media coverage" echoes the theme in [T4-009510](#T4-009510), which argues the New York Times' error in citing a fake Mike Flynn account undermines trust in its other reporting, and in [T4-008246](#T4-008246), which mocks outlets reporting on "fake news" as themselves unreliable. [T4-007115](#T4-007115) similarly questions the timing of information coming from the media and Democratic operatives, though it is framed as a quoted claim by Ann Coulter rather than the poster's own assertion. By contrast, [T4-005389](#T4-005389) urges caution against spreading "#fakenews" and deferring to "professionals," a stance closer to trusting established media gatekeepers than to the new post's generalized distrust, while [T4-008934](#T4-008934) attacks a specific reporter for "tip-toeing around the Truth" rather than questioning media reliability as a category. The new post is thus a vague, untargeted expression of distrust, whereas the retrieved posts mostly name specific outlets, individuals, or quote third parties.
